story_title: As an authorised internal user, I want to view venue availability over relevant dates and times so that I can identify when venues may be requested

acceptance_criteria.text: Users can select a venue and date/time period.
Availability is shown per fixed slot (AM, PM, Night) for each day, including slots occupied by setup or turnaround time.
Only authorised internal users can access the availability calendar.

open_questions: SCREEN BUILT, AND THESE CASES HAVE BEEN EXECUTED. When they were drafted the calendar screen (S-21) did not exist, and they were written against the acceptance criteria as its specification; the screen landed in the same commit. The wording they name ('View availability', 'Show availability', 'Venue', 'From', 'To', 'Previous week', 'Next week', 'Free', 'Booked', 'Turnaround', 'Unavailable', 'Closed', 'Limited hours', 'Approved bookings', 'Unavailable periods', 'Room in use', 'Overlaps with') was checked against src/app/venues/[id]/availability/page.tsx and matches. Executed 2026-09-26 against a running server, after merging main: 21 of the 22 pass and TC14 is not executable (see below). One wording note for TC11 - 'Classroom' is the screen's label for the stored value 'classroom' (layoutLabel(), page.tsx); the API itself carries the raw value.

EVERY DATE IN THIS FILE ASSUMES A DATABASE SEEDED ON 2026-09-20 - RE-BASE THEM BEFORE RUNNING. prisma/seed.ts builds every date as day(n) = the day it was run + n days, so each date named under Preconditions and Test Data moves with every reseed, and a tester following the steps against a later seed sees an empty grid and reports a bug that isn't one. Add (your seed day - 2026-09-20) days to every date here. Your seed day is the date `npx prisma db seed` was last run; to recover it from the data instead, the Jurong Expo Floor renovation period always begins on seed day + 21. Measured on 2026-09-26 the offset was +6 days: 5 Oct -> 11 Oct, 1 Oct -> 7 Oct, 11-17 Oct -> 17-23 Oct, 13 Oct -> 19 Oct, 23 Oct -> 29 Oct, 26 Oct -> 1 Nov, 3 Nov -> 9 Nov, 24 Nov -> 30 Nov, 30 Nov -> 6 Dec, 1 Dec -> 7 Dec, 2 Dec -> 8 Dec, 7 Dec -> 13 Dec, 8 Dec -> 14 Dec, 14 Dec -> 20 Dec. Recorded as a Known Gap in DOCUMENTATION.md: it affects every story's test cases, not just this one, and the fix needs a team decision.

Team decision - how users reach the calendar: a 'View availability' link on every row of the Venues list, and a 'View availability' button on the venue edit page. The Venues list link is the one that matters for Event Coordinators, who hold the calendar permission but cannot open the edit page - their Venues list is read-only and its rows do not click - so a link on the edit page alone would have left the role this story most serves (identifying when venues may be requested, ahead of SPM-42) with no way in except typing the address. TC16 reaches the calendar through the Venues list link.

AC5 cannot be tested by hand. Nothing in the app can create a venue unavailable period - the Block venue screen (S-23) is not built and nothing writes to that table - and the five seeded periods are at five different venues, so none overlap. TC14 needs two overlapping periods added to the demo data before it can run. Today AC5 is covered by unit tests only.

Team decision - slot boundaries: AM 06:00–12:00, PM 12:00–18:00, Night 18:00–23:00, no slot crossing midnight, the same grid for every venue. SPM-46 names the three slots but never defines their times, and nothing else in the project does, so the team set them. A venue's own opening hours mark a slot closed or partly open but do not move the boundaries: a fixed grid keeps venues comparable, and nothing defines where PM would start if AM started at each venue's opening time. AM starts at 06:00 rather than the first-proposed 08:00 because 08:00 was measured against the demo data and was too late: of 13 approved bookings, four fell partly outside the grid once setup time was added - up to 120 minutes each - because Jurong Expo Floor opens at 06:00 and Marina Grand Hall's 180-minute setup puts a 09:00 event in the room from 06:00. With AM at 06:00 all 13 fit the grid, and the Sundara Hospitality Trade Showcase went from 120 minutes outside to 0. TC07 and every expected slot in TC08-TC13 and TC19 rest on these times.

Team decision - 'confirmed bookings' in AC3 and AC7 means a booking whose own status is Approved, not a booking whose event is Confirmed. VenueBooking has no 'confirmed' status; Approved is the state that commits the room. The calendar exists to prevent double-booking, and the event-status reading was checked against the demo data and fails that: the Straits Medical Research Symposium booking at Marina Grand Hall on 1 Dec 2026 is approved while its event is still in Planning, so under the event-status reading the room would show as free and invite a second booking - discovered only at approval time, since this story blocks SPM-42. The event's status is still shown with each booking for information. TC19 is the case that proves this; TC20 and TC21 confirm pending, rejected and cancelled bookings do not block a slot.

Technical Support is internal staff, but cannot open the calendar (TC18) - the calendar reuses the venue catalogue's 'venue:view' permission, which Technical Support does not hold. AC6 says 'authorised internal users' without naming roles. Is excluding Technical Support intended?

What should a slot show when the room is open for only part of it? TC10 expects 'Free' with a 'Limited hours' note (One-North Rooftop Terrace opens at 16:00, so only 16:00–18:00 of PM is usable). The acceptance criteria do not cover opening hours at all.

The S-21 mockup (design/mockups/VenueCalendar.dc.html) shows a continuous hour-by-hour grid, pending requests and 'tentative holds'. AC2 asks for AM/PM/Night slots, and the team chose to follow AC2. Pending requests are deliberately not shown (TC20), and 'tentative hold' does not exist anywhere in the data. Confirm the mockup is superseded for this screen.

A booking whose room time falls outside every slot (between 23:00 and 06:00) would not appear in the grid at all. Nothing in the demo data does this today, so no case covers it. How should the screen warn about it?

Two checks the endpoint performs cannot be reached from a date picker and so have no test case: a date that does not exist (e.g. 31 Feb) and a date in the wrong format. The browser's date control cannot produce either.
